primitives.name: Abel Summation Method
primitives.verbatim_quote: (Hint: use Abel's method of partial summation.) What can be said if μ(E) = ∞, or if the summation is extended from n = 0?
primitives.assumptions: Function f is measurable; μ(E) may be infinite or summation extends beyond n=0.
primitives.breakdown_regime: When μ(E) = ∞ or summation range is unbounded, convergence behavior becomes ambiguous.

primitives.name: Measurable Set Intersection
primitives.verbatim_quote: (5) Suppose that {En} is a sequence of measurable sets and m is any fixed positive integer, and let G be the set of all those points which belong to En for at least m values of n.
primitives.assumptions: Each En is measurable; m is a fixed positive integer.
primitives.breakdown_regime: Failure occurs when intersection does not preserve measurability or when m exceeds countable bounds.

layer2.mapping: Maps to GSI event filtering logic where repeated membership defines probabilistic thresholds.
layer2.telemetry: Cardinality of shared elements across measurable sequences.

primitives.name: Non-Negative Function Integrability
primitives.verbatim_quote: Let f be a non negative integrable function on a measure space (X,Sμ).
primitives.assumptions: f is non-negative and integrable over X with respect to μ.
primitives.breakdown_regime: Integrability fails if f is not bounded or μ(X) is infinite without decay.

layer2.mapping: Supports GSE probabilistic state estimation via bounded expectation values.
layer2.telemetry: Integral value of non-negative functions over finite measure spaces.
